chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Jabala, from Hammad ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from his father, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, said:
Know that My houses on the earth are the mosques; they shine for the people of the sky as the stars shine for the people of the earth.
Know that good fortune is for those whose houses are the mosques.
Know that good fortune is for a slave who performs ablution in his house and then visits Me in My house.
Know that it is incumbent upon the Host to honor the guest.
Give glad tidings to those who walk in the darkness to the mosques with bright light on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for walking to the mosque in darkness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith qudsi emphasizes the ontological status of mosques as divine abodes, linking physical visitation with spiritual proximity. It specifically rewards the act of performing ablution at home before walking to the mosque, promising the 'radiant light' (*al-nur al-sati*) on Judgment Day, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the illumination of the faithful. This tradition underscores the merit of communal worship and the transformative power of consistent ritual practice in the believer's journey toward divine favor.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) says, “Know that Allah says, ‘

My houses on the earth are mosques. As stars provide light to the people on earth mosques do to the people on heaven. Know that those people have Tooba (good fortune) whose houses are mosques. Also know that a slave of Mine who performs ablution in his house and come to My house for meeting Me shall have Tooba (good fortune). Know that it is necessary for the host to honor his guest. Know that there are  glad tidings of bright light on the Day of Judgment for one who visits the mosque in darkness.
